html:
The Gumbaynggirr are an Aboriginal people of the mid north coast of New South Wales, with country from the Clarence River south to around Nambucca, and inland toward the New England tableland. Coffs Harbour lies in the middle of it.

Their coast gave fish, shellfish and the produce of rainforest and estuary. Neighbours were the Bundjalung to the north, the Dunghutti to the south and the Anaiwan on the tableland.

Cedar cutters arrived in the 1840s, followed by farmers, and the frontier brought killings. The Gumbaynggirr language survived in a few speakers, and since the 1980s a language cooperative at Nambucca Heads has led its revival, with dictionaries, school lessons and now a bilingual school. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
